approvalRequirements: Be an Austin Utilities residential customer at the service address.
Complete the required pre-audit questionnaire and schedule the CONSERVE & SAVE House Call.
Complete the selected audit and pay the applicable customer copay.
Provide access and any follow-up documentation or verification requested by Austin Utilities.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Austin Utilities publishes the House Call as a standard residential audit service with fixed customer copays and an administrative scheduling process rather than a competitive selection. An eligible customer who completes the questionnaire, scheduling, payment, and access requirements is likely to receive the audit, subject to program capacity.
reviews.evidenceText: Austin Utilities describes a residential whole-house House Call audit, requires a pre-audit questionnaire and scheduled appointment, and lists fixed customer copays. Program forms also provide for utility review, documentation, and verification.

approvalRequirements: Receive qualifying Avista residential service in Washington at the installation address.
Install a currently eligible measure in an eligible existing home and use an approved program contractor where required.
Submit the rebate claim, or receive the participating contractor's instant discount, with invoices and required product documentation.
Allow Avista or its program contractor to verify the installation if requested.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Avista publishes prescriptive residential rebates and contractor-delivered discounts with objective customer, equipment, invoice, and documentation rules. The process is administrative rather than competitively ranked, so a compliant claim is likely to be paid, subject to current measure availability and funds.
reviews.evidenceText: Avista's current Washington single-family page offers rebates for qualified installations, directs customers to apply with contractor invoices and supporting documents, and routes some insulation work through approved program contractors that provide an instant discount.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Avista nonresidential electric customer in Idaho.
Select a measure that meets the current prescriptive specifications or obtain Avista approval for a site-specific project.
Contact Avista before purchase or construction for site-specific or custom incentives and execute any required agreement.
Submit invoices, technical specifications, savings calculations, and other required completion documents.
Pass any required pre-installation or post-installation inspection.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The program combines published prescriptive incentives with site-specific incentives. Custom projects require early Avista involvement and project review, but the program is not described as competitively ranked; eligible, approved projects that document completion are likely to receive the authorized incentive.
reviews.evidenceText: Avista's Idaho business page offers prescriptive and site-specific incentives, caps site-specific incentives by project economics, and instructs customers to contact Avista before purchase because projects already under construction or completed without Avista involvement are not eligible for that path.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Avista nonresidential electric customer in Washington.
Select a measure that meets the current prescriptive specifications or obtain Avista approval for a site-specific project.
Contact Avista before purchase or construction for site-specific or custom incentives and execute any required agreement.
Submit invoices, technical specifications, savings calculations, and other required completion documents.
Pass any required pre-installation or post-installation inspection.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Avista's Washington business program provides published prescriptive incentives and an administratively reviewed site-specific path. Although custom projects need preapproval and verification, there is no published competitive ranking, so an eligible project that follows the required process is likely to receive its approved incentive.
reviews.evidenceText: Avista's current Washington business page offers prescriptive and site-specific incentives, requires Avista involvement before purchase for site-specific work, and excludes projects already under construction or completed without that involvement.

approvalRequirements: Receive qualifying Avista residential electric service in Idaho at the installation address.
Install a currently eligible measure that meets the listed home, fuel, equipment, and efficiency requirements.
Submit the current rebate application with itemized contractor invoices and required model or efficiency documentation.
Allow installation verification or inspection if requested.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Avista publishes objective residential rebate specifications and a post-installation documentation process. Claims are reviewed administratively rather than scored against competing applicants, so a complete eligible claim is likely to be awarded, subject to current program availability.
reviews.evidenceText: Avista's current Idaho single-family page provides rebates for qualified installations and directs customers to submit an application with contractor invoices and required supporting documentation.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Avista nonresidential customer receiving qualifying Washington gas or electric service for the measure.
Use equipment and measures that meet the current prescriptive rules or obtain site-specific project approval.
Contact Avista before purchase or construction for site-specific or custom incentives and execute any required agreement.
Submit invoices, technical documentation, and savings information required for the selected measure.
Pass any required inspection or installation verification.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current Avista Washington business offering includes prescriptive rebates and a custom/site-specific route. The latter requires project approval and verification, but awards are based on published eligibility and project economics rather than a competitive solicitation, making payment likely after approved completion.
reviews.evidenceText: Avista's Washington business page covers a broad set of gas and electric efficiency measures, requires advance contact for site-specific incentives, and conditions payment on project documentation and program review.

approvalRequirements: Be an Azusa Light & Water residential electric customer and city resident at the installation address.
Purchase and install an eligible residential EV charger at the Azusa service address.
Submit the signed application with a receipt or paid invoice showing the purchase date, model, quantity, and price within the stated claim period.
Obtain required permits and allow utility verification if requested.
Remain within the limit of one charger rebate per residence per year.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Azusa publishes a fixed residential EV charger rebate and objective documentation rules. Complete qualifying applications are processed as utility bill credits rather than competitively ranked awards, so approval is likely while program funds remain available.
reviews.evidenceText: The current Azusa program materials list a fixed EV charger rebate, a one-per-residence annual limit, customer and installation-address requirements, recent proof of purchase, a signed application, permit compliance, and possible verification. Funding is limited.

approvalRequirements: Own qualifying real property in Baltimore County and be liable for the county real property tax.
Obtain the required qualifying high-performance certification or rating, such as the applicable LEED or National Green Building Standard level.
Submit the county tax-credit application with certification, rating, and project documentation.
Receive approval from Baltimore County for the applicable certification level and credit period.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: This is a statutory county tax credit based on documented certification and an administrative application, not a competitively ranked grant. A property that satisfies the certification and filing rules is likely to receive the applicable credit after county review.
reviews.evidenceText: Baltimore County identifies separate high-performance building and home tax-credit paths and uses recognized certification or rating documentation to determine eligibility and the applicable credit. The credit applies to the county real property tax obligation.

approvalRequirements: Own qualifying real property in Baltimore County and be liable for the county real property tax.
Install a device that qualifies under the county's solar or geothermal energy-conservation-device rules; a generic high-efficiency HVAC replacement alone is insufficient.
Submit the county application with invoices, installation details, and required equipment or permit documentation.
File no later than June 1 of the year immediately preceding the first taxable year for which the credit is requested.
Receive county approval and allow inspection or additional verification if required.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The county credit is an objective, noncompetitive property-tax benefit for qualifying solar or geothermal devices. Approval is likely for a timely, documented application that meets the statutory device requirements, but the title's broad HVAC mapping does not make ordinary HVAC equipment eligible.
reviews.evidenceText: Baltimore County's current page requires the Energy Conservation Devices Tax Credit application by June 1 before the first taxable year. County law and forms limit the credit to qualifying solar and geothermal devices and require supporting installation information.

approvalRequirements: Have an eligible BGE residential account at the installation address.
Purchase or install a measure that meets the current equipment, efficiency, and home eligibility rules.
Use a participating contractor and complete an audit or modeled project scope where the Home Performance pathway requires it.
Submit the rebate claim or receive the point-of-sale discount with invoices, equipment documentation, and any required contractor forms.
Pass installation verification or inspection when required.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: BGE publishes prescriptive rebates, point-of-sale discounts, and a contractor-administered Home Performance path. These are administrative incentives rather than competitive awards, so an eligible customer with complete documentation is likely to receive the applicable rebate, subject to program terms and funds.
reviews.evidenceText: BGE's current residential pages list fixed rebates and discounts for eligible equipment and modeled Home Performance improvements, with customer-account, contractor, invoice, equipment, and verification requirements.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible BGE commercial, industrial, governmental, institutional, or nonprofit electric customer on a qualifying rate schedule.
Submit the application and supporting project information before starting work when using the custom-measure path.
Meet the current prescriptive specifications or demonstrate cost-effective verified energy savings for a custom project.
Receive the program approval letter before proceeding when preapproval is required.
Submit final invoices and completion documentation and pass any required site inspection.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: BGE's business program provides direct prescriptive incentives and a defined custom-review process. Custom projects require preapproval and verified savings, but the program is not a competitive solicitation; a qualifying approved project is likely to be paid after completion and verification.
reviews.evidenceText: BGE identifies eligible business rate schedules, offers prescriptive and custom incentives, and requires custom applications and supporting data before work begins, followed by approval, invoices, and possible pre- and post-installation inspections.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible BGE residential electric customer with an eligible EV or Level 2 charger.
Enroll through BGE's current EVsmart enrollment process and complete account and device eligibility verification.
Maintain the required vehicle or charger data connection and permit managed or off-peak charging as applicable.
Comply with the ongoing program and rate terms to earn bill credits or time-of-use savings.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current EVsmart offering is a managed-charging and EV time-of-use savings program, not the former upfront charger-installation rebate implied by the stale title. Eligible customers who successfully enroll and maintain device connectivity are likely to receive the published credits or rate savings, though ongoing benefits depend on participation and charging performance.
reviews.evidenceText: BGE's current EVsmart portal offers Vehicle Charging Time-of-Use and Smart Charge Management. It requires an eligible EV or charger, enrollment and verification, and ongoing connected or managed charging; the current offering does not present a general upfront installation rebate.

approvalRequirements: Be a Barron Electric Cooperative member and install the equipment on the cooperative's lines.
Purchase and install eligible commercial, industrial, or agricultural equipment during the current program year.
Submit the applicable 2026 form with an itemized receipt or invoice and required product, installation, or savings documentation within three months.
Submit by the published annual deadline and before program funds are depleted.
Allow cooperative inspection or additional verification if requested.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Barron Electric publishes current prescriptive forms and a standard claim process for members. Complete eligible claims are administratively reviewed and generally paid by bill credit or check, making an award likely while annual funds remain available.
reviews.evidenceText: Barron Electric's 2026 rebate page and forms require equipment to be installed on cooperative lines, current-year purchase and installation, timely forms and invoices, and measure-specific documentation. Funding is limited and the cooperative may inspect or limit payment.

approvalRequirements: Be a Barron Electric Cooperative member and install the charger on the cooperative's lines.
Use the cooperative-provided smart charger or an eligible alternative charger and comply with the required load-management period.
Coordinate with Barron Electric before or during installation when an alternative charger needs a cooperative radio receiver or other control equipment.
Submit the current EV rebate form with the charger receipt and proof of eligible vehicle purchase or registration.
Submit before the annual deadline and while funds remain available.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The cooperative publishes a current fixed charger incentive and a defined administrative claim process. An eligible member who coordinates required control equipment, accepts load management, and submits complete documentation is likely to receive the incentive while funds remain.
reviews.evidenceText: Barron Electric's 2026 EV form offers a cooperative smart charger or an alternative-charger incentive, requires installation on cooperative lines, load-management participation, receipts and vehicle documentation, and advance coordination for certain alternative chargers.

approvalRequirements: Be a Barron Electric Cooperative member and install the measure on the cooperative's lines.
Purchase and install a currently eligible appliance, HVAC, water-heating, lighting, or audit measure during the program year.
Use pre-coordination or an approved provider where the measure, such as an energy audit, requires it.
Submit the applicable 2026 form with a receipt or invoice and required ENERGY STAR, AHRI, efficiency, or installation documentation within three months.
Submit by the annual deadline and allow inspection if requested.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Barron Electric's current offerings are prescriptive member rebates with objective forms and documentation. Although some measures require advance coordination and all payments remain subject to funds and verification, a compliant claim is likely to be approved.
reviews.evidenceText: The cooperative's 2026 page and forms require current-year eligible equipment on cooperative lines, timely claims, receipts and efficiency documentation, and measure-specific coordination. Rebates are limited by available funds and may be inspected.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Bartholomew County REMC residential member at the installation address.
Install a currently qualifying heat pump, geothermal system, or water-heating measure that meets the published efficiency rules.
Submit the current installation application with an itemized invoice and required model, AHRI, or efficiency documentation.
Allow REMC inspection and receive utility approval before the incentive is issued.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Bartholomew County REMC currently publishes residential installation applications and an administrative approval process. The cooperative reserves approval and inspection rights, but a member with qualifying equipment and complete documentation is likely to receive the applicable incentive.
reviews.evidenceText: The REMC's current incentives page lists residential heat-pump and water-heater installation applications. The applications condition payment on qualifying equipment, supporting information, utility review, and possible inspection.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Southern California Edison business customer on a qualifying time-of-use or real-time-pricing rate.
Have qualifying monthly demand and be able to reduce load by at least the program minimum, including at least 100 kW and the required percentage reduction.
Submit and receive approval of the BIP contract, select a Firm Service Level and notification option, and have the required interval meter.
Pass the pre-enrollment performance test.
Reduce load to the contracted Firm Service Level during called events to retain credits and avoid penalties.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: BIP enrollment and credits depend on site-specific demand, a material curtailable-load commitment, contract approval, and a successful performance test. These are not merely paperwork conditions, and ongoing payments depend on actual event performance, so award likelihood is possible without customer load and test data.
reviews.evidenceText: SCE describes BIP as a contracted demand-response program for large business customers. Eligibility includes demand and curtailable-load thresholds, an interval meter, an approved contract, a pre-enrollment test, and continued event performance for monthly bill credits.

approvalRequirements: Own qualifying business equipment in Maine that is otherwise eligible for the Business Equipment Tax Exemption and first subject to tax in an eligible year.

For a battery system, document that more than 50 percent of electrical output serves behind-the-meter load at the site, or document a fully executed utility interconnection agreement dated on or before January 1, 2025.
File the annual BETE application and equipment schedule with the local assessor by May 1, unless a valid good-cause extension is granted.
Provide valuation, placed-in-service, ownership, location, and other documentation requested by the assessor.
Receive assessor approval for the exemption.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Maine law expressly makes qualifying battery systems eligible for the statutory BETE exemption and uses an annual assessor application rather than competitive selection. A timely application that satisfies the battery-use or grandfathered-interconnection test is likely to be approved after assessor review.
reviews.evidenceText: Maine Revenue Services states that BETE is a property-tax exemption for qualifying business equipment. Current 2025 legislation clarifies battery-system eligibility and changes the application deadline to May 1, with limited good-cause extensions by the assessor.

approvalRequirements: Own or control an eligible multifamily property of at least five units in the nine-county Bay Area and within the applicable utility service area.
Submit the BAMBE Interest and Eligibility Form and be confirmed eligible by the program.
Work with the assigned technical assistant, complete a site visit and Energy Survey Report, and develop a qualifying multi-measure scope with the required modeled savings.
Reserve the rebate before purchasing equipment or starting construction.
Complete the approved scope, submit final documentation, and pass the post-installation site visit.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: BAMBE requires property and project screening, a technical-assistance process, a qualifying multi-measure savings scope, and rebate reservation before construction. Funding is limited and not every interested property proceeds to reservation, so an unreviewed project has only a possible award even though accepted reserved projects follow a defined payment process.
reviews.evidenceText: BayREN's current BAMBE process requires an interest and eligibility form, technical assistance, a site visit, a multi-measure qualifying scope, and rebate reservation before purchase or construction. Final payment follows documentation and a post-installation site visit.

approvalRequirements: Live in an eligible single-family home of four or fewer units in a participating Bay Area county, built before 2010, and receive PG&E service.
Meet the household-income limit of no more than 120 percent of area median income and submit acceptable verification.
Include at least one qualifying weatherization measure in the project scope.
Obtain property-owner permission when the applicant is a tenant.
Complete the program assessment, approved scope, participation documents, and installation through the program process.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: EASE Home is an income- and property-qualified program with objective threshold rules and a managed project process, not a competitively ranked grant. Once eligibility and the required weatherization scope are confirmed, an applicant who completes the program steps is likely to receive the approved subsidy, subject to program capacity and funds.
reviews.evidenceText: BayREN's current EASE Home page requires a home of four or fewer units built before 2010, PG&E service, household income at or below 120 percent of area median income, and at least one weatherization measure. Tenants need owner permission.

approvalRequirements: Submit the online BeSMART loan application with the required employment, income, and borrower information.
Obtain financial preapproval through DHCD's credit and income review.
Submit an eligible project scope, contractor estimates, and required ENERGY STAR or equipment specifications.
Use a Maryland-licensed and insured contractor and provide the contractor documentation requested by DHCD.
Receive project approval, sign and notarize the loan documents, and obtain the initial funding draw before starting work.
Submit completion certificates and other closeout documentation for final disbursement.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: BeSMART is a loan rather than an entitlement rebate. Approval depends on borrower financial underwriting and project-specific review in addition to ordinary paperwork, so an applicant's likelihood is only possible until income, credit, contractor, and scope information are approved.
reviews.evidenceText: Maryland DHCD requires an online application, income and financial preapproval, project specifications and contractor estimates, project approval, and signed notarized loan documents before the initial draw. Final funds follow completion documentation.

approvalRequirements: Be a Beaches Energy Services commercial electric customer at an existing commercial property in its service territory.
Contact the conservation specialist before installation and submit the retrofit worksheet and lighting analysis for review.
Use a Florida-licensed contractor, obtain required permits, and install qualifying lighting equipment in accordance with manufacturer requirements.
After approval and installation, submit the completed rebate application with proof of purchase or installation within 90 days.
Pass any required on-site verification.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Beaches Energy publishes a formula-based commercial lighting rebate with objective customer, pre-review, contractor, permit, invoice, and inspection rules. It is not competitively ranked, so a project approved before installation and properly documented afterward is likely to receive the bill credit.
reviews.evidenceText: The current Beaches Energy page lists a commercial lighting rebate up to the published cap. The official form requires pre-installation specialist review, an existing commercial property, licensed work and permits, an application and invoice within 90 days, utility approval, and possible inspection.

approvalRequirements: Be the Beaches Energy Services residential customer of record at an existing primary residence in its service territory.
Purchase and install a currently listed qualifying home-upgrade measure that meets the measure-specific efficiency and installation rules.
Use licensed contractors and obtain permits where required by the measure.
Submit the completed rebate form with dated proof of purchase or installation and required equipment documentation within 90 days.
Allow on-site installation verification if requested.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Beaches Energy offers fixed prescriptive residential rebates and a clear administrative claim process. An eligible customer who installs a listed measure and submits complete documentation within 90 days is likely to receive the bill credit, subject to program terms.
reviews.evidenceText: Beaches Energy's current page lists residential rebates for HVAC, water heating, insulation, and window measures and requires forms and proof of purchase within 90 days. Official forms limit eligibility to existing primary residences served by the utility and permit inspection.

approvalRequirements: Be the Beaches Energy Services residential customer of record at an existing primary residence in its service territory.
Install a new Florida Solar Energy Center-certified domestic solar water-heating system that replaces an electric water heater.
Use a Florida-licensed contractor, obtain required permits, and meet the program's code, shading, sizing, and freeze-protection requirements.
Submit the completed rebate form and contractor invoice within 90 days of installation.
Allow on-site inspection before the rebate is issued if requested.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The solar-water-heater rebate is a fixed prescriptive utility credit with detailed objective system and documentation rules. A qualifying installation with a timely complete application is likely to receive the credit after administrative review and any requested inspection.
reviews.evidenceText: The current Beaches Energy page lists a solar water-heater rebate. The official form requires an FSEC-certified new domestic system, licensed installation and permits, replacement of an electric water heater, timely invoice-backed application, and possible inspection.

approvalRequirements: Be a Belmont Light residential customer and install the battery at a residential service address.
Complete the Standard Interconnection Application process and obtain required permits or interconnection approvals before energization.
Submit the Battery Storage System Rebate application at interconnection or after installation, but within six months of installation.
Provide the installer, equipment, installation, and account documentation requested by Belmont Light.
Receive Belmont Light review and approval.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Belmont Light currently publishes a fixed residential battery rebate and a defined interconnection and application process. The benefit is not competitive; an eligible system that completes interconnection and submits a timely complete claim is likely to receive the bill credit after utility review.
reviews.evidenceText: Belmont Light's current battery page offers a fixed annual residential bill credit, requires the Standard Interconnection Application process, permits filing at interconnection or after installation, and requires the rebate application within six months for utility review and approval.
